identity.name: Lohara dynasty
alt_names: Kingdom of Kashmir under the Lohara dynasty

land.text: Kashmir: Didda 'adopted as her heir' her nephew Samgrāmarāja, 'From this decision arose the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir'

predecessors.note: Didda page; Lohara infobox 'Preceded by: Utpala dynasty'.

land.text: the Valley and its hills, taken by Shah Mir in 1339: 'he threw her and her children in prison while he himself ascended the throne as Sultan Shamsu'd-Din Shah'

successors.note: Shah Mir ended 'the last remnants of the Lohara dynasty' (Lohara page); 'The Shah Miris ruled from 1339' (Sultanate page). Cliopatria's Kashmiri Sultanate row starts in 1344. The Sultanate page's infobox lists Rinchan Shah (Sadr'ud-Din) as its first sultan, 1320-1323, and the years 1323-1339 as the 'Lohara Interruption'; this dossier follows kashmir.json and the Lohara page, which count Rinchan as a usurper inside the same realm (a rename) and end the realm in 1339.

capitals.name: Srinagar
capitals.note: Lohara infobox 'Capital: Srinagar'. The fortress of Loharkot in the Pir Panjal was the original seat of the Lohara line and 'At this point the fortress became the dynastic seat' after Utkarsa's accession in 1089; the page dates no move of the court. Coordinates as the Kashmir dossier's Srinagara.

rulers.name: Ananta
rulers.note: start inferred from his predecessor's end (the page prints no years); forced to abdicate in 1063 in favour of his son Kalaśa, d. 1081

rulers.name: Kalaśa
rulers.note: 'was king until 1089'; Ananta kept the real power until 1081

rulers.name: Harsa
rulers.note: murdered by dāmaras in 1101; Utkarsa held the throne briefly in 1089 (no years printed)

rulers.name: Uccala
rulers.note: start from the page's 'again split at the time of Uccala's accession' (1101); 'downfall of Uccala came in December 1111'

rulers.name: Sussala
rulers.note: abdicated in favour of his son Jayasimha in 1123; Bhiksacara 1120-early 1121 interrupts; Jayasimha 'succeeded his father in 1128'

rulers.name: Paramanuka
rulers.note: no years printed; bounded by Jayasimha's end and Vantideva's start

rulers.name: Vantideva
rulers.note: 'ruled 1165-72', 'often described as the last king of the Lohara dynasty'

rulers.name: Vuppadeva
rulers.note: no years printed; succeeded in 1181 by Jassaka

rulers.name: Rāmadeva
rulers.note: became king in 1252; Laksmandeva's reign began in 1273

rulers.name: Laksmandeva
rulers.note: began 1273; Simhadeva came to the throne in 1286

rulers.name: Suhadeva
rulers.note: fled to Kishtwar in the Zulju raid of 1320

rulers.name: Rinchan (Sadr'ud-Din Shah)
rulers.title: Ladakhi usurper
rulers.note: 'claimed the throne for himself in 1320 and reigned until 1323'; not of the Lohara line (he converted to Islam in December 1320, Sultanate page).

rulers.name: Udayanadeva
rulers.note: Suhadeva's brother, 'invited back to rule after Sadr-ud-Din's death' (Lohara page); 'The rule of Udayanadeva lasted until his death in 1338' (Sultanate page).

rulers.name: Kota Rani
rulers.title: queen
rulers.note: succeeded her husband Udayanadeva in 1338; Shah Mir 'threw her and her children in prison' and took the throne in 1339.

correction.text: as 1227: Kashmir Valley and its hills, outline carried over because the pages date no change between 1236 and 1301

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1260-1293: Cliopatria's Lohara row ends in 1259 but the Lohara page lists kings to 1320 (Rāmadeva from 1252, Laksmandeva from 1273, Simhadeva 1286-1301, Suhadeva 1301-1320); the Kashmir Sultanate page says Kashmir 'became a Mongol dependency some time after 1235'. The page gives no extent for these decades, so the 1227 outline is carried (confidence 1, page silent). Cliopatria's own Kashmir row has no shape for 1236-1293 either.

correction.text: as 1227 without the Ladakh, Xinjiang and Xizang land that Cliopatria's Kashmir row adds in 1294 (the Kashmir dossier's kashmir_1294)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1294-1339: the years after Cliopatria's Lohara row ends (1259) and to the Shah Mir takeover of 1339 (extended from 1320 when the dossier's end moved to match kashmir.json; the shape is unchanged because the pages date no change across Zulju's raid, Rinchan and the Lohara return). Area check: the corrected shape resolves to 318 cells, about 80,000 km2 (Jammu and Kashmir 149 cells, Himachal Pradesh 98, Azad Kashmir 43, the rest Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa), against Cliopatria's Kashmir row of 201,709 km2 and the Sultanate infobox's 222,236 km2 for 1342 (ratio 2.8, so the drawn shape is about a third of the infobox figure). The infobox belongs to the Sultanate and its extent note reads '(Including the hill states of Gilgit and Jammu, Maqpon Kingdom and Maryul Kingdom as tributary states)'; of Baltistan (Maqpons) and Ladakh (Maryuls) the page says 'Direct control was not established over these territories'. The correction therefore leaves out Gilgit-Baltistan, Ladakh, Xinjiang and Xizang, which is most of the difference, and 1342 also lies after this dossier's end. The Sultanate page names only 'the Valley' as the realm that passed to local chiefs when Suhadeva fled in 1320.

region.text: Kashmir, where Didda's nephew was her heir

ledger.note: 1003: Didda dies and her nephew Samgrāmarāja founds the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir. Didda 'ruled as Queen regnant from 980 until her death in 1003' (8 August 1003); her nephew was adopted as heir and 'From this decision arose the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir'; Lohara infobox 'Established: 1003', 'Preceded by: Utpala dynasty'. The page gives 'Kashmir', not a boundary.

region.text: Lohkot Fort, Tosa Maidan, Kashmir (the Lohara page: the fortress of Loharkot in the Pir Panjal, present-day Poonch district)

ledger.note: 1015: Mahmud of Ghazni besieges Lohkot. 'The Siege of Lohkot took place in A.D. 1015 during the reign of Mahmud, the ruler of the Ghaznavid Empire'; infobox 'Summer - Winter 1015', 'Lohkot Fort, Tosa Maidan, Kashmir'; defenders the Lohara dynasty under Sangramaraja. The Lohara page places Loharkot in the present-day Poonch district; the circle is my reading of that.

region.text: Lohkot Fort, Tosa Maidan

ledger.note: 1015: Mahmud abandons the siege and retreats to Ghazni, the result 'inconclusive'; he lost much of his army to attrition and winter. No change of control in Kashmir.

region.text: Lohkot Fort, Tosa Maidan

ledger.note: 1021: Mahmud returns to Lohkot. 'Mahmud, having not yet given up on Kashmir, led a second military campaign in 1021 AD' to overcome the fortress of Loharkot.

region.text: Lohkot Fort, Tosa Maidan

ledger.note: 1021: winter again defeats the Ghaznavids and Mahmud 'gave up on further plans of expansion into Kashmir'. The page reports no change of control.

region.text: the Jammu and Pir Panjal hills that leave the Kashmir row in 1056, the Valley excluded (about 53 cells)

ledger.note: 1056: Cliopatria's Kashmir shape loses its Jammu and Pir Panjal side. The Lohara page names no loss under Ananta, Kalaśa or Harsa and describes no frontier; recorded only so that the corrected keyframe of 1056 is explained (page silent).

region.text: Lohara, the fortress and its hills in the Pir Panjal (present-day Poonch district)

ledger.note: 1089: Utkarsa's accession reunites Kashmir with Lohara. 'With the accession of Utkarsa to the throne of Kashmir came the kingdom's reunification with Lohara'; Utkarsa 'was already ruler of Lohara'. The page ties the accession to the death of Kalaśa in 1089 and gives no boundary for Lohara beyond the fortress.

region.text: Lohara, ceded by Uccala to Sussala

ledger.note: 1101: Kashmir and Lohara part again. 'The two kingdoms of Kashmir and Lohara were again split at the time of Uccala's accession' (Harsa was murdered by the dāmaras in 1101); Uccala ceded 'rule over Lohara to Sussala'.

region.text: Lohara rejoined to Kashmir under Sussala

ledger.note: 1111: Sussala, who held Lohara, takes Kashmir. 'The downfall of Uccala came in December 1111' and Sussala 'proceeded to take control of Kashmir from a half-brother, Salhana'; the page gives no date for the takeover, so 1111 is the year of Uccala's fall (page silent on the rest).

region.text: the Jammu and Pir Panjal hills added to the Kashmir row in 1152

ledger.note: 1152: Cliopatria widens the Kashmir shape by about 199 cells (Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal). Jayasimha ruled to 1155 ('lasted until 1155'); the page dates no acquisition (page silent).

region.text: the foothills that join the Kashmir row in 1210

ledger.note: 1210: the Pothohar and Punjab foothills join Cliopatria's Kashmir shape (about 61 cells). The Lohara page is silent on these years (Jagadeva reigned 1199-1212 or 1213); recorded so the corrected keyframe is explained (page silent).

region.text: Kashmir, which 'became a Mongol dependency some time after 1235'

ledger.note: 1235: Kashmir becomes a Mongol dependency. 'Unable to fend off the invasions this time, Kashmir became a Mongol dependency some time after 1235.' The page gives no year after 1235 (confidence 1, bridging a silence). Written from the vassal's side as the 2026-10-19 review asked: this realm is the dependency and the Mongol Empire the suzerain; mongol-empire (ia-02) should carry the mirror with this realm as its counterpart. The Lohara page adds that 'a territorial encroachment by mongols troubled' Laksmandeva's reign, which began in 1273.

region.text: Kashmir, the Valley

ledger.note: 1320: Zulju's Mongols enter Kashmir. 'In 1320, a Mongol commander, Zulju, with an army of Qara'unas, entered Kashmir'; the raid ended Suhadeva's rule in the Valley.

region.text: Kashmir, the Valley

ledger.note: 1320: Zulju leaves with loot after widespread violence; the Valley is left to local chiefs and then Rinchan.

region.text: the Valley, from which Suhadeva fled when the Valley 'passed on to the hands of local chiefs who asserted independence'

ledger.note: 1320: the Mongol dependency is taken to end. The Sultanate page does not say when or how the dependency ended; the only later statement is that in 1320, as Suhadeva fled to Kishtwar, the Valley 'passed on to the hands of local chiefs who asserted independence'. 1320 is a bridge over that silence (confidence 1).

region.text: the Valley, taken by the Ladakhi noble Rinchan

ledger.note: 1320: Rinchan, a Ladakhi noble, takes the throne from the Lohara king Suhadeva (Zulju's raid had driven Suhadeva to Kishtwar). Lohara page: Rinchan 'claimed the throne for himself in 1320 and reigned until 1323'; he converted in December 1320 as Sultan Sadr'ud-Din (Sultanate page). Colour and dossier continue, as in kashmir.json /ledger/22; this replaces the earlier dissolve of 1320.

region.text: the Valley, back under the Lohara line

ledger.note: 1323: the Lohara line returns. The Sultanate page's infobox lists the 'Lohara Interruption: 1323-1339'; the Lohara page says Suhadeva's brother Udayanadeva was invited back after Sadr-ud-Din's death, and 'The rule of Udayanadeva lasted until his death in 1338' (Sultanate page). Colour and dossier continue, as in kashmir.json /ledger/23.

region.text: the Valley, where Shah Mir rose against Kota Rani

ledger.note: 1338: the Shah Mir-Lohara war begins. Infobox 'Shah Mir-Lohara War: 1338-1339'; after Udayanadeva's death in 1338 'Kota Rani appointed Bhatta Bhikshana, a powerful minister, as her Prime Minister, ignoring Shah Mir'.

region.text: the Valley

ledger.note: 1339: Shah Mir wins. He 'threw her and her children in prison while he himself ascended the throne as Sultan Shamsu'd-Din Shah' (the page gives no month).

region.text: the Valley and its hills under Kota Rani, passing to Shah Mir

ledger.note: 1339: Lohara rule ends and the Shah Mir sultanate begins. 'The Shah Miris ruled from 1339' (Sultanate page); Shah Mir ended 'the last remnants of the Lohara dynasty' (Lohara page, no date). The Lohara infobox's 'Disestablished 1175' contradicts its own text and is not used. Replaces the dissolve of 1320 (the Valley's fall to Zulju and Rinchan), which kashmir.json treats as a rename.

wars.name: Ghaznavid expeditions against Kashmir
wars.outcome: Both Ghaznavid sieges of Lohkot (1015, 1021) failed to the fortress and the winter; Kashmir kept its independence and Mahmud 'gave up on further plans of expansion into Kashmir'.
wars.note: After the 1013 campaign 'A significant portion of the Shahi kingdom was annexed to Mahmud's empire' (same page); the Lohara page adds that Samgrāmarāja 'supported Shahis of Gandhara against Ghaznavid attacks' (undated within 1003-1028).

wars.name: Civil strife of Harsa, Uccala and Sussala
wars.outcome: Uccala and Sussala 'forced to flee in 1100'; Harsa murdered by the dāmaras in 1101; Kashmir and Lohara split under Uccala; Uccala's fall in December 1111 and Sussala's takeover of Kashmir.
wars.note: Internal; no territorial zone beyond the Kashmir-Lohara split of 1101 recorded in the ledger.

wars.name: Zulju's raid on Kashmir
wars.outcome: The raid ends Suhadeva's rule: he flees to Kishtwar, the Valley passes to local chiefs, then Rinchan Shah.

wars.name: Shah Mir-Lohara war
wars.outcome: Shah Mir deposes Kota Rani and takes the throne in 1339, ending the Lohara line.
wars.note: Infobox 'Shah Mir-Lohara War: 1338-1339'; the page gives no battle and no month.

certainty.note: Mountain frontiers of a kingdom whose pages name only places (Srinagar, Loharkot, the Valley); nothing is sharp.

notes:
WHAT THIS ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'Lohara Dynasty' row (1003-1259, 15 shapes) is not the Lohara realm as the pages describe it. Its three outlines are a ring of 597, 762 and 765 cells (about 175,000 to 226,000 km2) over Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Xinjiang, Ladakh, the Pamirs (Gorno-Badakhshan) and Badakhshan, with the Kashmir Valley missing or nearly missing in 1003-1055 (7 of 56 cells) and 1152-1259 (5 of 56). The Lohara page names only Srinagar (capital), the fortress of Loharkot in the Pir Panjal ('present-day Poonch district of Jammu') and 'Kashmir'. The same ring is Cliopatria's Utpala row (marked wrong in the utpala-dynasty dossier). I follow that dossier and the kashmir dossier: the Lohara line ruled the same Kashmir kingdom as the Karkotas and Utpalas, so every shape is corrected to the land the kashmir dossier draws for the same years (Kashmir Valley plus Cliopatria's Kashmir row without Xinjiang, Ladakh and Baltistan). RECOMMENDATION for the colour agent and reviewer: treat lohara-dynasty as a dynasty period of the state 'kashmir' (this dossier keeps its own ledger so that it validates alone); draw the territory once, from the kashmir dossier, never both.

ENDS (repaired 2026-10-19). The dossier now ends in 1339 to match kashmir.json: 1320 (Zulju's raid, Suhadeva's flight to Kishtwar, Rinchan) is a rename, the Lohara line returns in 1323 (Udayanadeva, then Kota Rani from 1338) and Shah Mir takes the throne in 1339 ('The Shah Miris ruled from 1339'; the Lohara page: he ended 'the last remnants of the Lohara dynasty'). The Lohara infobox says Disestablished 1175 (Vantideva 1165-72 is 'often described as the last king'), the rulers list runs to Suhadeva 1301-1320, History of Kashmir quotes 'the Lohara dynasty (1003-1320 CE)' and the Sultanate page lists Rinchan as its first sultan (1320-1323) and 1323-1339 as the 'Lohara Interruption'; the pages disagree, and 1339 is the choice that keeps one realm with one end. Cliopatria's 1259 is too early, and the Sultanate row starts in 1344.

MONGOL DEPENDENCY (repaired). Kashmir 'became a Mongol dependency some time after 1235' (Sultanate page). The vassal_start (1235, confidence 1) and a bridged vassal_end (1320, confidence 1) are now in this ledger, written from the vassal's side with counterpart mongol-empire as the review asked; the schema describes vassal events from the suzerain's side, so mongol-empire (ia-02) should carry the mirror. The page does not say when the dependency ended.

MERGE INTO KASHMIR (open, orchestrator). lohara-dynasty and utpala-dynasty duplicate kashmir.json (another sa-03 part; I may not edit it). To fold: add 'Lohara Dynasty' to kashmir.json identity.cliopatria_names; move the 17 keyframe verdicts (lohara-dynasty_1003 ... _1294, the last two being new keyframes 1260-1293 and 1294-1339) and the Lohara-principality events (1089 gain, 1101 split, 1111 merge) and the Mongol vassal pair (1235, 1320) into kashmir.json; kashmir.json already has the 1003 rename, the 1015-1021 sieges, the 1056/1152/1210 steps, the 1320 raid and rename, the 1323 return and the 1339 dissolve; then retire this file. Until then the colour/render agents must draw the Valley from ONE of the three.

LOHARA PRINCIPALITY. The 1089 gain, 1101 split and 1111 merge name 'Lohara principality' (Poonch; no boundary on any page, drawn as a 50 km disc at Loharkot). If Lohara is folded into kashmir.json the events can stay as they are or be recorded as internal; if not, the principality needs a dossier (reported under counterparts_needing_dossiers). The Lohara page says Didda entrusted Lohara to Vigraharaja while Samgramaraja took Kashmir (undated).

PAGES THAT FAILED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayasimha_of_Kashmir and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayasimha_(Kashmir) (URL_NOT_FOUND), so Jayasimha's reign (1128-1155), the dāmara revolts and Gulhana as king of Lohara are only what the Lohara page says. The Harsha page is thin and gives no territory. Not settled: any territory outside the Valley and the Pir Panjal; the Jammu, Rajauri, Kishtwar and Chamba frontiers (no page names them); Shahi alliance (undated). The 1056, 1152 and 1210 events are confidence-1 mirrors of the kashmir dossier's, kept only to explain the corrected keyframes. Cross-check from the review: kara-khitans /ledger/12 gives 218 Pamir cells to lohara-dynasty, but the corrected 1152 shape removes the Pamirs, so that Kara-Khitan loss should go to 'nobody' (ia-01).
